title: Hacker Uses DeepSeek AI to Autonomously Attack Servers
content_md:
Hacker Uses DeepSeek AI to Autonomously Attack Servers

A Chinese-language threat actor is using the DeepSeek AI model and the open-source Hermes Agent to conduct autonomous cyberattacks on vulnerable servers with minimal human involvement.

Unit 42 identified an autonomous AI-driven hacking campaign conducted by a Chinese-language threat actor. They attacked infrastructure using seven vulnerabilities, combining AI-driven autonomous enumeration with manual exploitation, achieving confirmed impact.

The actor, operating under the pseudonyms knaithe and KnYuan, used DeepSeek via the Hermes Agent platform as an autonomous offensive operator. They orchestrated this operator via Telegram for the following actions: independent target enumeration and vulnerability discovery using FOFA, acquiring exploit tools, and initiating attacks without human intervention.

Alongside using DeepSeek as an autonomous operator platform, the actor configured multiple large language models (LLMs) including Qwen, GLM, Kimi, and MiniMax. Researchers also observed limited use and testing of Western platforms, including Claude Code for connectivity testing and proxy validation, and signs of Codex use in exploit development directories.

When initial exploitation failed due to restrictive target environment configurations, the Hermes agent autonomously searched for known critical vulnerabilities (CVEs). It initially searched 10 product families, scanning GitHub for popular proof-of-concept exploits and prioritizing vulnerabilities by attack surface. This research led the agent to focus on higher-value vulnerabilities, seven of which are documented. Although the observed campaign had limited impact, the workflow confirms a functional, comprehensive, autonomous offensive capability.

Source: https://linuxiarze.pl/haker-uzywa-glebokiej-sztucznej-inteligencji-do-autonomicznego-atakowania-serwerow/
